summary.short: Recast EU directive setting minimum rules for re-use of existing documents held by public sector bodies, public undertakings and publicly funded research data. Sets free-of-charge re-use with cost-based exceptions, generally prohibits exclusive rights, and requires APIs for dynamic and high-value datasets. Member States transpose by 17 July 2021.
summary.long: Directive (EU) 2019/1024 recasts Directive 2003/98/EC on re-use of public sector information. It sets minimum rules for re-use of existing documents held by public sector bodies, by public undertakings in listed sectors, and of publicly funded research data already in public repositories (Art. 1). Re-use is free of charge, with charges limited to marginal costs; listed bodies may charge more under cost-based criteria, with return on investment capped at 5 percentage points above the ECB fixed rate (Art. 6; Art. 2(16)). Conditions must be non-discriminatory (Art. 11), and exclusive rights are generally barred, subject to exceptions (Art. 12). Dynamic data must be available via APIs immediately after collection (Art. 5). Implementing acts will designate high-value datasets from six Annex I categories, to be free of charge and provided via APIs (Art. 13-14). Member States must adopt open access policies for research data (Art. 10). Requests are processed within 20 working days, extendable (Art. 4). Transposition is due by 17 July 2021, and Directive 2003/98/EC is repealed from that date (Art. 17, 19).

‘public sector body’ means the State, regional or local authorities, bodies governed by public law or associations formed by one or more such authorities or one or more such bodies governed by public law;
‘bodies governed by public law’ means bodies that have all of the following characteristics:
‘public undertaking’ means any undertaking active in the areas set out in point (b) of Article 1(1) over which the public sector bodies may exercise directly or indirectly a dominant influence
‘university’ means any public sector body that provides post-secondary-school higher education leading to academic degrees;
‘standard licence’ means a set of predefined re-use conditions in a digital format, preferably compatible with standardised public licences available online;
any content whatever its medium (paper or electronic form or as a sound, visual or audiovisual recording); or
‘anonymisation’ means the process of changing documents into anonymous documents which do not relate to an identified or identifiable natural person
‘dynamic data’ means documents in a digital form, subject to frequent or real-time updates
‘research data’ means documents in a digital form, other than scientific publications, which are collected or produced in the course of scientific research activities
‘high-value datasets’ means documents the re-use of which is associated with important benefits for society, the environment and the economy
‘re-use’ means the use by persons or legal entities of documents held by:
‘personal data’ means personal data as defined in point (1) of Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679;

‘machine-readable format’ means a file format structured so that software applications can easily identify, recognise and extract specific data, including individual statements of fact, and their internal structure;
‘open format’ means a file format that is platform-independent and made available to the public without any restriction that impedes the re-use of documents;
‘formal open standard’ means a standard which has been laid down in written form, detailing specifications for the requirements on how to ensure software interoperability;

‘reasonable return on investment’ means a percentage of the overall charge, in addition to that needed to recover the eligible costs, not exceeding 5 percentage points above the fixed interest rate of the ECB;
‘third party’ means any natural or legal person other than a public sector body or a public undertaking that holds the data.

obligations.summary: Public sector bodies process re-use requests electronically where possible, within a reasonable time (no fixed time limits apply where none are set elsewhere: 20 working days, extendable by 20 working days for extensive or complex requests, with notice within three weeks); communicate grounds for refusal; include a reference to means of redress in re-use decisions; and establish practical arrangements to facilitate re-use.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to requests for re-use; Art. 4(6) exempts public undertakings and educational, research performing and research funding organisations.

evidence.quote: Public sector bodies shall, through electronic means where possible and appropriate, process requests for re-use

obligations.summary: Public sector bodies and public undertakings make documents available in any pre-existing format or language, by electronic means where possible, in open, machine-readable, accessible, findable and re-usable formats together with metadata, complying with formal open standards where possible. Art. 5(7) applies this to existing documents held by public undertakings.
obligations.conditional_on: Where possible and appropriate; no duty to create or adapt documents where this involves disproportionate effort (Art. 5(3)).

obligations.summary: For identifying specific high-value datasets, the Commission carries out appropriate consultations including at expert level, conducts an impact assessment including a cost-benefit analysis, and ensures complementarity with existing legal acts.
obligations.conditional_on: For the purpose of identifying specific high-value datasets under Art. 14(1).

evidence.quote: the Commission shall carry out appropriate consultations, including at expert level, conduct an impact assessment

obligations.summary: Member States may exempt public sector bodies required to generate revenue from the requirement to make high-value datasets available free of charge for no more than two years after the implementing act enters into force, where this would substantially impact their budget.
obligations.conditional_on: Where free availability would lead to a substantial impact on the budget of the bodies involved; period of no more than two years following the entry into force of the relevant implementing act.

evidence.quote: Member States may exempt those bodies from the requirement to make those high-value datasets available free of charge

obligations.summary: Conditions of the delegation to the Commission: delegation for five years from 16 July 2019 with tacit extension; the Commission reports at least nine months before expiry; the Commission consults experts designated by each Member State before adopting a delegated act and notifies it simultaneously to Parliament and Council.
obligations.conditional_on: Delegation under Art. 13(2).

evidence.quote: The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period.

obligations.summary: Member States bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with the Directive, communicate them to the Commission, and communicate the text of the main provisions of national law adopted in the field.

evidence.quote: Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 17 July 2021.

obligations.summary: The Commission carries out an evaluation of the Directive and submits a report to Parliament, Council and the EESC; Member States provide the Commission with the information necessary for that report.

evidence.quote: No sooner than 17 July 2025, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Directive

enforcement.note: No penalty, fine, criminal, licence, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking provision found. Article 4(4) and Article 7(3) provide means of redress (review by an impartial review body), not sanctions. Article 17 requires transposition only, and Article 21 addresses Member States.
